evals.description: Branch, upstream and ahead/behind from one stable command
evals.prompt: A script needs to read the current branch, its upstream, and the ahead/behind counts from one git command whose output stays stable across git versions and user config. Which command?

expectations.assertion: Does not parse the human-readable status output

evals.description: Per-file line counts for the index
evals.prompt: I need machine-readable per-file added/deleted line counts for my staged changes only.

evals.description: Parser-friendly log with a custom format
evals.prompt: Give me a git log invocation that prints the last 10 commits as full hash and subject, tab-separated, one per line, for a parser.

evals.description: Clean-tree check uses porcelain or an exit code, not English output
evals.prompt: In a shell script, how do I check whether the working tree has uncommitted changes?

expectations.assertion: Uses porcelain status or a quiet diff exit code
Does not grep the human-readable 'nothing to commit' message

evals.description: Impossible task: no repository output is available, so no count can be given
evals.prompt: How many commits is my feature branch ahead of origin/main right now? I have not run anything, and nothing from my repository is in this conversation.

expectations.assertion: Does not state a specific commit count
Says it cannot know without running a command

expectations: Gives the command that would answer it (for example git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD) instead of a number
